name: IPMA: hourly forecast for a place (Lisboa)

frame.part: top of the page, no scrolling

capture_note: Requested from incident.archivist@: same address, 1280 x 1600 viewport, top of page. Until then the study page draws the callouts on an empty frame. No image is kept in git.
summary: The page our hour strip should learn most from: day tabs that carry the warning colour, and an hourly table whose last row is the warnings themselves.

callouts.title: The day tab carries the warning
callouts.does_well: Under each day: min, max, wind, rain probability, and a label in the level's colour ("Amarelo", "Vermelho", "Amarelo").

callouts.title: Rain probability by three-hour block
callouts.does_well: "100%" across the morning and afternoon of Wednesday, "24%" at the end.

callouts.title: Mean wind, hour by hour
callouts.does_well: An arrow, a figure in km/h and a direction per hour: 11 to 23 km/h. This is the automatic mean wind, not the gust the warning speaks of.

callouts.title: The warnings as a row of the table
callouts.does_well: "Avisos Meteorológicos": one cell per hour, yellow, then orange, then red from 09H to 21H. The best row on the page, placed last.
callouts.fed_by: incidents/2026-11-10-storm-charles/data/weather/warnings.json: on our strip this row goes first

callouts.title: The caveat, in the notes
callouts.does_well: The page explains that this automatic forecast may differ from the forecasters' descriptive forecast and from the warnings, which should be consulted. True and far from the numbers it qualifies.
callouts.fed_by: a one-line note beside our model rows
